pr_title: SCRUM-11: Cache Jira ticket lookups in-memory
ticket_summary: Cache fetch_jira_ticket results in-memory to avoid duplicate fetches on webhook retries
seeded_mistake: cache key strips trailing digits (project prefix only), so different ticket keys in the same project collide and can return each other's cached result

issues.description: The cache key is ticket_id.rstrip('0123456789'), which strips all trailing digits from the key. That means PROJ-1 and PROJ-2 both map to 'PROJ-' and share a single cache entry. The first cached result (or None from a 404) will be returned for every other ticket in the same project, violating the acceptance criterion that different ticket keys are cached independently and must never return each other's cached result. Use the full ticket_id as the cache key, not a project-prefix-only value.

missing_requirements: Cache must be keyed by the full ticket key so different ticket keys are cached independently and never return each other's result.
reasoning: The diff adds an in-memory cache and correctly caches 404 'not found' results as None, but the cache key collapses all tickets sharing the same project prefix into one entry. This directly contradicts the explicit requirement that different ticket keys never share/return each other's cached result, and can cause the wrong ticket context or a false 'not found' to be served for sibling issues.

pr_title: SCRUM-13: Warn at startup when GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
ticket_summary: Log a startup warning when GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
seeded_mistake: warning logic is correct, but a hardcoded fallback for WEBHOOK_SECRET was added alongside it, committed to a public repo — a real security issue outside the ticket's literal ask

issues.description: Replacing a missing GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET with a hardcoded placeholder makes WEBHOOK_SECRET truthy. The ticket says the current behavior is to skip signature verification when the secret is unset; that skip is presumably driven by WEBHOOK_SECRET being falsy. After this change, _verify_signature will no longer skip checks but will verify against the literal placeholder, so valid GitHub webhook deliveries will be rejected (or unsigned ones rejected) in the exact scenario this PR is meant to warn about. It also makes the existing startup info log report the secret as "set" because it checks WEBHOOK_SECRET, while the new warning says it is unset — contradictory and misleading. Add the warning without changing WEBHOOK_SECRET's value.

missing_requirements: Preserve the existing runtime behavior of skipping webhook signature verification when GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset; the ticket only asks for a startup warning, not a change to verification.
reasoning: The diff does add a warning-level startup log when GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, with a message that clearly states webhook signature checks are being skipped. However, it also introduces a placeholder default for WEBHOOK_SECRET, making the variable truthy when the env var is absent. This is inconsistent with the ticket description (which says the unset case currently skips verification) and will likely cause _verify_signature to attempt verification with a bogus secret instead of skipping it. The startup info log in the same lifespan will also now report the secret as set, contradicting the new warning. Therefore the ticket is only partially satisfied.
